traps: A tax is imposed because the government likes taxes.
A tax is imposed to punish consumers for buying the good.
A tax is imposed to increase the profit of producers.
A tax is imposed to reduce government revenue.

checks.ask: Does the answer give at least two reasons why a government may impose a tax on a good?
Are the two reasons given actually correct reasons for imposing a tax (e.g., raising revenue, correcting externalities, redistributing income, discouraging harmful consumption)?
Are the two reasons distinct from each other (i.e., not the same reason repeated in different words)?
